title: Undefined date on altair chart hovering
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary There is this weird bug on latest versions of streamlit where yearmonth(date) in an altair chart displays undefined as a value when you hover it. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import datetime from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta import streamlit as st import pandas as pd import altair as alt date_now = datetime.datetime.now() date_last_month = datetime.datetime.now() - relativedelta(months=1) data = [ {"user": 1, "date": date_now}, {"user": 2, "date": date_now}, {"user": 3, "date": date_now}, {"user": 4, "date": date_last_month}, {"user": 5, "date": date_last_month}, {"user": 6, "date": date_last_month}, ] df = pd.DataFrame(data) chart = ( alt.Chart( df, title=alt.TitleParams( "undefined bug", anchor="middle", ), ) .mark_bar() .encode( x=alt.X("yearmonth(date):N", title="Mois"), y=alt.Y("count():Q", title="Effectif"), ) ) st.altair_chart(chart) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Update streamlit to 1.55.0. 2. Run the code. 3. You see undefined instead of the month. ### Expected Behavior You should see the expected month from the dataframe. ### Current Behavior ### Is this a regression? - [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.55.0 - Python version: 3.12.3 - Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04 noble - Browser: Chrome (v146.0.7680.71) ### Additional Information It used to work fine on streamlit 1.52.2.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-14361)

This is a bug report for a regression in `st.altair_chart` where using `yearmonth(date):N` (time unit with nominal encoding) displays "undefined" instead of formatted date labels (e.g., "February 2025"). The user confirms this worked in Streamlit 1.52.2 but broke in 1.55.0. The most likely root cause is the **vega-lite upgrade from 6.3.1 to 6.4.2** (introduced via [PR #13023](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/13023)). Vega-lite 6.4.0 introduced a tooltip newline feature ([vega-lite#9678](https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/pull/9678)) that caused a regression where tooltip data shows `"undefined"` instead of actual values. While vega-lite 6.4.2 includes a fix ([vega-lite#9707](https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/pull/9707)), the fix may not cover all cases — particularly time unit transforms with nominal encoding combined with Streamlit's mark config (`tooltip: { content: "encoding" }`) and/or the AST expression interpreter (`vega-interpreter`) used for CSP compliance.

### Related Issues

- **[#12390](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12390)** — Regression in v1.49.0 where tooltips in layered Altair charts stop showing when a facet encoding is used inside `st.dialog`. Both issues involve Altair chart tooltip/rendering regressions potentially tied to upstream vega-lite changes.
- **[#5733](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5733)** (closed) — Previous issue where `st.altair_chart` showed blank axis/chart when provided a datetime domain, fixed by updating `vega-interpreter`. Demonstrates a pattern of datetime rendering issues caused by vega dependency incompatibilities.
- **[#4342](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4342)** (closed) — Previous issue where tooltip and axis labels displayed incorrect dates for `st.altair_chart`. Same category of date formatting issues in Altair charts within Streamlit.
